topic.subject: physics
topic.title: Electromagnets and magnetic devices
topic.scopeBasis: TGS 2025-26: magnets and magnetism; TGS 2026-27: electromagnets
topic.overview: Electric current produces a magnetic field. Coiling the wire and adding an iron core concentrates and strengthens the field, creating a controllable magnet.
learningGoals: Recall the precise Year 8 scientific vocabulary and symbols.
Apply the idea to an unfamiliar example rather than relying on recognition.
Use the command word, show working where needed and include every mark point.
mustMemoriseRules: A current in a wire produces a magnetic field around the wire.
A solenoid is a coil of wire whose field resembles a bar magnet's field.
An iron core inside a current-carrying solenoid strengthens the electromagnet.
Increasing current or the number of turns per length generally strengthens the field.
An electromagnet is switchable because its field depends on current.
Reversing current reverses the solenoid's north and south poles.
Electromagnets are used in relays, electric bells, speakers and scrapyard cranes.
A fair strength test changes one factor, controls the others and uses a repeatable measure such as maximum identical paper clips lifted.

mustMemoriseVocabulary.meaning: a magnet produced by current, usually in a coil with an iron core
material placed inside a coil to affect its magnetic field
one loop of wire in a coil
electrically operated switch using an electromagnet
able to be turned on and off
direction of conventional charge flow determining field orientation
test in which only the chosen independent variable changes

workedExamples.prompt: How can a scrapyard crane release metal?
workedExamples.answer: Switch off the electromagnet's current so its field collapses.

workedExamples.prompt: Predict the effect of doubling coil turns while controlling current and core.
workedExamples.answer: The electromagnet should become stronger, within equipment limits.

practicals.title: Electromagnet strength
practicals.aim: Investigate one factor affecting electromagnet strength.
practicals.variables: IV: number of turns, current or core; DV: maximum identical paper clips lifted; controls: all other coil/core/supply factors and contact time.
practicals.method: Build a low-voltage coil around an iron nail, vary one factor systematically, energise for equal times, count clips lifted and repeat.
practicals.expectedResult: More turns/current or an iron core generally increases strength.
practicals.safety: Use low voltage, switch off between trials and stop if wire or battery becomes hot.
practicals.evaluation: Repeat, calculate means, use identical clips and recognise that heating can change current.

commonMistakes: Saying current is unnecessary once an electromagnet is on.
Using a steel permanent core when quick demagnetisation is required without discussion.
examTips: Strength factors: current, turns and iron core.
State what is changed, measured and controlled.
For a device, describe both the circuit action and magnetic action.
beforeStartingPractice: Read the key rules once, cover them, then retrieve them aloud or in writing.
Use MC first for confidence, but finish with typed, calculation, practical or explanation evidence.
After an error, study the explanation; the same concept returns later in a different format and again after 2 and 7 days.

practicals.subject: physics
practicals.title: Electromagnet strength
practicals.aim: Investigate one factor affecting electromagnet strength.
practicals.variables: IV: number of turns, current or core; DV: maximum identical paper clips lifted; controls: all other coil/core/supply factors and contact time.
practicals.method: Build a low-voltage coil around an iron nail, vary one factor systematically, energise for equal times, count clips lifted and repeat.
practicals.expectedResult: More turns/current or an iron core generally increases strength.
practicals.safety: Use low voltage, switch off between trials and stop if wire or battery becomes hot.
practicals.evaluation: Repeat, calculate means, use identical clips and recognise that heating can change current.
